knowledge_point.title: Solving for Two Coefficients in a Linear Combination

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}-6 \\ 2 \\ -3\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-6 \\ 2 \\ -3\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1} \\ -{x}_{1} \\ 2{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-6 \\ 2 \\ -3\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} \\ 2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-6 \\ 2 \\ -3\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=-6 \\ -{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=2 \\ 2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} &=-3\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Adding the first and the second equations we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{2} &=-4 \\ {x}_{2} &=2\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${x}_{2}=2$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=-6 \\ {x}_{1}-(2) &=-6 \\ {x}_{1} &=-4 \\ {x}_{1} &=-4\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=-4$ and ${x}_{2}=2$ into the third equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} &=-3 \\ 2(-4)+3(2) &=-3 \\ -2 &=-3\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a false statement.

So, the system has no solution.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{c}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 4 \\ 4\end{bmatrix},\,{c}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\,d=\begin{bmatrix}13 \\ -7 \\ 7\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{c}_{1}+{x}_{2}{c}_{2}=d,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
.
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{c}_{1}+{x}_{2}{c}_{2}=d$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 4 \\ 4\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}13 \\ -7 \\ 7\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1} \\ 4{x}_{1} \\ 4{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}2{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}13 \\ -7 \\ 7\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} \\ 4{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} \\ 4{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}13 \\ -7 \\ 7\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=13 \\ 4{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=-7 \\ 4{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} &=7\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Adding the second and the third equations we get

$$
\begin{aligned}8{x}_{1} &=0 \\ {x}_{1} &=0\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${x}_{1}=0$ into the third equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} &=7 \\ 4(0)+{x}_{2} &=7 \\ {x}_{2} &=7 \\ {x}_{2} &=7\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=0$ and ${x}_{2}=7$ into the first equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=13 \\ (0)+2(7) &=13 \\ 14 &=13\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a false statement.

So, the system has no solution.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}7 \\ 8 \\ 4\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}7 \\ 8 \\ 4\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}4{x}_{1} \\ -2{x}_{1} \\ 3{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}7 \\ 8 \\ 4\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}4{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} \\ -2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}7 \\ 8 \\ 4\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=7 \\ -2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} &=8 \\ 3{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=4\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Multiplying the third equation by $-1$ and adding the result to the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} &=3\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${x}_{1}=3$ into the third equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=4 \\ 3(3)-{x}_{2} &=4 \\ -{x}_{2} &=-5 \\ {x}_{2} &=5\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=3$ and ${x}_{2}=5$ into the second equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} &=8 \\ -2(3)+3(5) &=8 \\ 9 &=8\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a false statement.

So, the system has no solution.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}-7 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}-20 \\ 10 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}-7 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-20 \\ 10 \\ 0\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}3{x}_{1} \\ -3{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-7{x}_{2} \\ 5{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-20 \\ 10 \\ 0\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}3{x}_{1}-7{x}_{2} \\ -3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{1}-{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-20 \\ 10 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}-7{x}_{2} &=-20 \\ -3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2} &=10 \\ {x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=0\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Adding the first and the second equations we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{2} &=-10 \\ {x}_{2} &=5\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${x}_{2}=5$ into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2} &=10 \\ -3{x}_{1}+5(5) &=10 \\ -3{x}_{1} &=-15 \\ {x}_{1} &=5\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=5$ and ${x}_{2}=5$ into the third equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=0 \\ (5)-(5) &=0 \\ 0 &=0\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement.

So the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=5$ and ${x}_{2}=5$, which means

$$
5{a}_{1}+5{a}_{2}=b.
$$

Consequently,

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=(5)+(5)=10.
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ -3 \\ 5\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}7 \\ -15 \\ 23\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ -3 \\ 5\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}7 \\ -15 \\ 23\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1} \\ -2{x}_{1} \\ 3{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}2{x}_{2} \\ -3{x}_{2} \\ 5{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}7 \\ -15 \\ 23\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} \\ -2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}7 \\ -15 \\ 23\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=7 \\ -2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2} &=-15 \\ 3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2} &=23\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Multiplying the first equation by $2$ and adding the result to the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} &=-1\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${x}_{2}=-1$ into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2} &=-15 \\ -2{x}_{1}-3(-1) &=-15 \\ -2{x}_{1} &=-18 \\ {x}_{1} &=9\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=9$ and ${x}_{2}=-1$ into the third equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2} &=23 \\ 3(9)+5(-1) &=23 \\ 22 &=23\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a false statement.

So, the system has no solution.
